data.text:
The government has failed to remit billions in mandated revenues to PhilHealth, creating massive arrears that undermine Universal Health Care. Between 2023 and 2025 alone, PhilHealth faced a cumulative deficit of over ₱356 billion due to withheld sin tax shares and diverted PAGCOR/PCSO funds. 
Reference :
Senate of the Philippines website 

https://t.co/rzFD2sm2m5

🔎 Breakdown of Government Arrears to PhilHealth

1. Legal Violations of Sin Tax and UHC Laws

• Sin Tax Law (RA 11346, 2019) requires:• 40% of tobacco & sweetened beverage taxes
• 60% of alcohol taxes
• 50% of PAGCOR & PCSO revenues
→ All earmarked for PhilHealth.

• Universal Health Care Act (RA 11223) mandates PhilHealth as the single payor system.
• These provisions are legal obligations, not discretionary allocations. Senate of th...

2. Budgetary Defunding

YearPhilHealth Requirement
Actual Allocation      
Deficit
2023₱136.8B₱50.7B.  ₱86.1B
2024₱129B.   ₱9.5.         ₱119.5B
2025₱151B.    ₱30M.         ₱151B

➡ Total deficit (2023–2025): ₱356.6B 

https://t.co/kTc61iQYkX

3. Non-Remittance of Earmarked Revenues

• Sin Tax Shortfalls: In 2023, only ₱79.2B was allocated, far below the ₱136.8B mandate.
• PAGCOR & PCSO: Required 50% remittance, but ₱21B (2023) and ₱21.22B (2024) were diverted. No clear remittances in 2025–2026. BusinessWorl...

4. Supreme Court Ruling (Dec 5, 2025)

• Ordered government to return ₱60B illegally diverted in 2024 from PhilHealth to flood control and DOH debts.
• However, the 2026 budget “returns” this money via new tax collections, meaning citizens themselves repay what was taken — compounding the injustice. Senate of th...

5. Rise of MAIFIP & Patronage Politics

• DOH’s ₱51B MAIFIP fund rivals PhilHealth’s role, fragmenting financing.
• DOLE’s ₱25B “political ayuda” and DSWD’s ₱63B social welfare programs further dilute UHC’s single-payor principle.
• These discretionary funds enable patronage politics, weakening accountability and transparency. 

⚠️ Why This Matters

• Triple Violation:

1. Defunding PhilHealth against Sin Tax & UHC laws.
2. Failure to remit mandated revenues.
3. Patronage-driven parallel programs undermining UHC.

• Impact: Over 106 million Filipinos are cheated of their right to healthcare, eroding trust in institutions and replacing rights-based financing with politically driven allocations.
